chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the expiation for game, when its owner eats from its meat, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'He eats from his sacrifice (udhiyah) and gives the expiation (fid'ah) in charity.'

key_terms.أُضْحِيَّتِهِ: His sacrifice (specifically the animal offered for expiation)
key_terms.فِدَاءِ: Expiation (compensation for breaking a ritual constraint)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating the meat of the sacrificial animal used for hunting expiation?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of the expiation (fid'ah) for hunting, distinguishing between the animal itself and its compensatory value. While the hunter is permitted to consume the meat of the sacrificial animal (udhiyah) used as the expiation, the monetary equivalent or additional charity (sadaqah) derived from the fid'ah must be given to the poor. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance that the expiatory animal serves both as a ritual sacrifice and a source of sustenance for the offender, while the financial penalty remains strictly charitable.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about an expiation for the hunting, its owner eating from its meat’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can eat from his sacrifice, and he should give in charity with the expiation’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Flammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the expiation because of hunting; if one paying the expiation can eat thereof. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can eat from his offerings and he must give the expiation as charity.’”
